fam_driptape.scope_population_subset: Yields cover the hectares in each block that came to harvest
fam_driptape.scope_population_whole: Yields cover every hectare in each block, with unharvested ground entered at zero
fam_driptape.scope_completeness_complete: and every hectare in each block was harvested
fam_driptape.scope_completeness_incomplete: and about a quarter of each block's hectares went unharvested
fam_driptape.neutral_closer: Tonnages were entered to one decimal place and countersigned by the recording agronomist.
fam_driptape.note_stated_confound: All four blocks sit on one farm in one summer, so a single rainfall record covers every case at once. The mid-passage facts state that rainfall in each block's season ran to roughly double the year before and that every block lay in open ground, taking rain as it fell, so the extra water reached every block whose yield was measured. Each block is compared against itself a season earlier rather than against an undripped block in the same season, so the rain and the drip line moved together and the 0.4 to 0.7 tonne gains cannot be attributed to the line. The population and completeness clauses in the same line describe a tally with no gap between the ground measured and the ground the claim covers, so the rainfall is the whole of the defect.
fam_driptape.concerns: (1) Banned word in a clause I was told not to edit: confound_scope_block for this family reads 'and every block lay under a rain shelter, fed ONLY by metered water'. 'only' is on the requirement-6 prohibition list and appears in the TRUE-side scope clause, giving that variant a lexical marker the reach variant lacks. Recommend 'fed by metered water alone' or 'fed from a metered line' if the clause is ever reopened. (2) No causal connectives found in confound_fact_changed / confound_fact_same / either scope clause. (3) Unit fit: the cases report 'tonnes per hectare', so hectares-within-block is the natural tally unit and SUBSET (harvested hectares) is genuinely narrower than WHOLE (all hectares, failures at zero) — excluding failed ground inflates the per-hectare average, which is exactly the gap the FALSE cell needs. (4) Metadata drift in the existing file, not something I changed: the coherent_true 'notes' field says the closer holds 'mean temperature' fixed, but no temperature appears anywhere in the passage.

fam_fertilizer.scope_population_subset: Heights cover the plants in each plot that survived to the final measure
fam_fertilizer.scope_population_whole: Heights cover every plant fed in each plot, with losses entered at zero gain
fam_fertilizer.scope_completeness_complete: and every plant fed in each plot survived to that measure
fam_fertilizer.scope_completeness_incomplete: and close to a quarter of each plot's fed plants did not survive
fam_fertilizer.neutral_closer: Heights were entered in centimetres and copied into the notebook the same day.
fam_fertilizer.note_stated_confound: All four plots sit in the same backyard in the same summer, so one weather history covers every case at once. The mid-passage facts state that rainfall in each plot's season was the highest on record, roughly double the year before, and that every plot stood in the open, watered by rain alone, so that water reached every plot whose heights were taken. Each plot is compared against itself a year earlier rather than against an unfertilized plot in the same year, so the rain and the fertilizer moved together and the 8 to 13 cm gains cannot be attributed to the fertilizer. The population and completeness clauses in the same line describe a tally with no gap between the plants measured and the plants the claim covers, so the rainfall is the whole of the defect.
fam_fertilizer.concerns: (1) Salience asymmetry in a clause I was told not to edit, and it is the exact asymmetry the audit flagged: confound_fact_changed opens 'Rainfall in each plot's season was the HIGHEST ON RECORD, roughly double the year before' while confound_fact_same is the flat 'matched the year before to within a few millimetres'. 'Highest on record' is a superlative amplifier with no counterpart on the same side, so the changed variant reads louder than the same variant independent of any logic. This family is the loudest of my four on that axis. Recommend dropping 'was the highest on record,' so the fact clause is simply 'Rainfall in each plot's season ran to roughly double the year before' — which is what fam_driptape already does. (2) No causal connectives in the confound clauses. 'watered by rain alone' is not on the banned list ('only' is; 'alone' is not) and reads as exposure description rather than flagging, so I left it. (3) Unit fit caveat: the case sentences name a single specimen per plot ('a tomato in the Ellis backyard', 'an oak in the Aldergate orchard'), while my population clauses tally over 'the plants in each plot'. This reads as the plot's planting and is not contradictory, but if the builder wants a tight fit the case nouns could be pluralised ('tomatoes in the Ellis backyard'). Flagging rather than editing, since case sentences are out of my scope.

fam_inhaler.scope_population_subset: Counts cover the patients in each group who returned a symptom diary
fam_inhaler.scope_population_whole: Counts cover every patient prescribed in each group, with non-returners taken from clinic charts
fam_inhaler.scope_completeness_complete: and every patient prescribed in each group returned a diary
fam_inhaler.scope_completeness_incomplete: and about a quarter of each group's patients returned no diary
fam_inhaler.neutral_closer: Attack counts were entered as whole events and countersigned by the duty clinic supervisor.
fam_inhaler.note_stated_confound: All four groups are the 12-17 band at Harrowfield inside one winter quarter, so a single district air history covers every case at once. The mid-passage facts state that pollen and airborne irritants in each group's district fell by half from the previous quarter and that every group lived and slept in unfiltered district air, so the cleaner air reached every patient whose attacks were counted. Each band is compared against itself a quarter earlier rather than against an untreated band in the same quarter, so the drop in irritants and the inhaler moved together and the 4 to 7 attack reductions cannot be attributed to the inhaler. The population and completeness clauses in the same line describe a count with no gap between the patients tallied and the patients the claim covers, so the drop in irritants is the whole of the defect.
fam_inhaler.concerns: (1) Confound clauses are clean: no causal connectives, no banned hedges, and the changed/same fact pair ('fell by half' / 'held level with') is well matched for loudness — this family is the best-balanced of my four on the salience axis. (2) The SUBSET group here is the strongest of my four: diary non-return in an asthma cohort plausibly correlates with symptom severity in either direction, so the narrower group is genuinely non-representative rather than a relabelling, and the WHOLE variant's chart-review provision is a realistic way for a tally to cover everyone. (3) Metadata drift in the existing file, not something I changed: the coherent_true 'notes' field describes the closer as blocking a halving of pollen with 'filtered indoor air', but that item's passage actually states irritants 'held level' and groups breathing 'unfiltered district air'; the diverse_true 'notes' field has the mirror-image error, saying irritants 'held level' when its passage says 'fell by half'. The passages match the family_spec variants correctly — the notes are what is stale.

fam_labkit.scope_population_subset: Completion rates cover the students in each section who stayed enrolled to term's end
fam_labkit.scope_population_whole: Completion rates cover every student registered in each section, with leavers entered as non-completions
fam_labkit.scope_completeness_complete: and every student registered in each section stayed to that point
fam_labkit.scope_completeness_incomplete: and roughly a quarter of each section's registered students withdrew mid-term
fam_labkit.neutral_closer: Rates were recorded to the nearest point and signed off by the teaching office.
fam_labkit.note_stated_confound: All four sections sit at Harlow in one autumn term, so a single change to the central syllabus covers every case at once. The mid-passage facts state that the central syllabus doubled coursework's share of the final grade against the previous year and that every section was marked to that central syllabus, so the heavier weighting applied to every section whose completion was measured. Each section is compared against itself a year earlier under the old share, so the kit and the doubled share moved together and the 6 to 11 point rises cannot be attributed to the kit. The population and completeness clauses in the same line describe a tally with no gap between the students counted and the students the claim covers, so the syllabus change is the whole of the defect.
fam_labkit.concerns: (1) Confound clauses are clean: no banned causal connectives and no hedges. 'The central syllabus doubled coursework's share' is agentive but not one of the prohibited constructions, and the changed/same pair ('doubled ... against the previous year' / 'left ... at the previous year's') is well matched for loudness. (2) Word-count parity is exact here (population 14/14, completeness 11/11). (3) Wording note: I used 'leavers entered as non-completions' rather than 'withdrawals entered as non-completions' in the WHOLE clause to avoid the 'with withdrawals' stutter when it sits next to the INCOMPLETE clause, which uses 'withdrew mid-term'; the link between the two is still explicit. (4) The SUBSET group is genuinely non-representative: coursework completion measured over students who stayed to term's end excludes precisely the students least likely to have completed, so the reported rate is upward-biased relative to the claim's population — a stronger gap than a simple reporting-coverage story.

fam_nestbox.scope_population_subset: Counts cover the installed boxes that were inspected
fam_nestbox.scope_population_whole: Counts cover every installed box, uninspected ones entered as zero
fam_nestbox.scope_completeness_complete: and every installed box at each plot was inspected
fam_nestbox.scope_completeness_incomplete: and a fifth of the installed boxes at each plot went uninspected
fam_nestbox.neutral_closer: Ring numbers and box references were filed with the monitoring register under standard warden codes.
fam_nestbox.note_stated_confound: All four plots sit on one reserve, with one species in one spring under one warden, so the single fact stated mid-passage covers every case at once: prey abundance on the surrounding farmland doubled from the previous year, which is an alternative cause of higher fledgling counts. The scope clause beside that fact puts every box at the farmland edge, within the birds' foraging range, so the food surge reaches every brood that was counted. Each plot is measured against the same reserve a year earlier rather than against an unboxed wood in the same spring, so nothing in the evidence separates the boxes from the prey peak. The population and completeness clauses in the same line leave the tally covering the whole set of installed boxes, so they add no second defect.
fam_nestbox.concerns: The existing confound clauses carry no causal connectives. Two things worth flagging. (1) The REACH/BLOCK pair here ('within the birds' foraging range' / 'beyond the birds' foraging range') is a mechanism gloss rather than a bare location fact, so it does more explanatory work than the scope clauses in the other three families I was assigned; a reader who reaches it has been handed the reason the prey fact matters. If salience parity across families matters, consider 'at the farmland edge' / 'deep inside the reserve' with the foraging-range gloss dropped. (2) My clauses avoid naming the warden and use the passive 'were inspected', because the coherent item has one warden (Trask) and the diverse item has four; an active phrasing would need singular/plural to differ across conditions. The WHOLE variant enters uninspected boxes as zero, which understates the current year against the prior-year baseline, so WHOLE+INCOMPLETE stays conservative for an 'increase' claim rather than manufacturing one.

fam_onboarding.scope_population_subset: Retention figures cover the signups who confirmed an address
fam_onboarding.scope_population_whole: Retention figures cover every signup, unconfirmed ones counted as lost
fam_onboarding.scope_completeness_complete: and every signup in each cohort confirmed an address
fam_onboarding.scope_completeness_incomplete: and a third of each cohort's signups never confirmed an address
fam_onboarding.neutral_closer: Retention figures were exported to the analytics warehouse in the team's standard reporting schema.
fam_onboarding.note_stated_confound: All four cohorts are starter signups from Norway via webinar inside one March window, so the trial fact stated mid-passage covers every case at once: the free trial ran thirty days, four times its length in the earlier period, and a thirty-day trial leaves users still inside their trial at week two. The scope clause beside that fact has every cohort here signed up on that trial, so the policy change reaches all four. Each cohort is compared against itself a month earlier, when the seven-day trial still applied, so the longer trial and the onboarding email moved together and the 3 to 6 point lifts cannot be attributed to the email. The population and completeness clauses in the same line leave the retention figures covering every signup, so the trial length is the whole of the defect.
fam_onboarding.concerns: The existing confound clauses carry no causal connectives. Two notes. (1) This family's coherent_false depends on a step the passage never states, that a thirty-day trial keeps users active at week two; that inference is world knowledge, whereas the scope mechanism is entirely text-internal. The mid-passage move does not close that gap, so if the audit re-scores salience this item may still read differently from a scope-family item. (2) My SUBSET qualifier is address confirmation, which the onboarding email itself can prompt, making the narrower group post-treatment. That strengthens rather than weakens SUBSET+INCOMPLETE, but if a treatment-independent qualifier is preferred, substitute 'Retention figures cover the signups whose accounts the tracker matched' / 'Retention figures cover every signup, unmatched accounts counted as lost' / 'and the tracker matched every account in each cohort' / 'and the tracker missed a third of the accounts in each cohort'; those are 10/10/9/12 words and read across all four combinations.

fam_reading.scope_population_subset: Scores cover the pupils in each class who sat the paper
fam_reading.scope_population_whole: Scores cover every pupil on roll, non-sitters entered at their previous mark
fam_reading.scope_completeness_complete: and every pupil on each class roll sat it
fam_reading.scope_completeness_incomplete: and a quarter of each class roll did not sit
fam_reading.neutral_closer: Marks were transcribed onto the district return sheet and filed under the standard class codes.
fam_reading.note_stated_confound: All four classes are Year 4 groups at Ashcombe Primary in one autumn term taught by Vance, so the single fact stated mid-passage covers every case at once: class sizes at each school fell by half from the year before. The scope clause beside that fact has every logged class taking its English lessons as one whole group, so every lesson was delivered to half as many pupils as in the term the class is measured against. Each class is compared against itself in the previous autumn term, when the groups were twice the size, so the evidence cannot separate the smaller classes from the reading program. The population and completeness clauses in the same line leave the scores covering every pupil on roll, so no second defect is present.
fam_reading.concerns: No causal language in the existing confound clauses, but the draft file has two metadata errors in its notes fields that a reviewer reading notes rather than passages would be misled by. In items/draft/fam_reading.json, coherent_true's notes claim 'every class took its English lessons in fixed groups of six' while its passage carries 'as one whole group' (same_reach), and diverse_true's notes claim 'class sizes matched the year before' while its passage says they 'fell by half' (changed_block). The passages and the confound_variant fields both agree with family_spec.json, so the defect is confined to the notes prose. Separately, the BLOCK clause 'in fixed groups of six' is a partial rather than a clean block: halved rolls could still change marking load and teacher attention outside English lessons, so the CHANGED+BLOCK item is less airtight than the BLOCK clauses in fam_sleepapp or fam_onboarding. Finally, my completeness clauses talk about class rolls while the confound fact talks about class sizes; the two are compatible and never contradict, but the mid-passage line does mention roll size twice in adjacent clauses.

fam_sleepapp.scope_population_subset: Readings cover the enrolled users whose devices synced
fam_sleepapp.scope_population_whole: Readings cover every enrolled user, unsynced ones held at baseline
fam_sleepapp.scope_completeness_complete: and every enrolled user's device synced in each cohort
fam_sleepapp.scope_completeness_incomplete: and a fifth of the enrolled devices in each cohort never synced
fam_sleepapp.neutral_closer: Heart rates were recorded in beats per minute and filed in the clinic's standard format.
fam_sleepapp.note_stated_confound: All four cohorts are 40 Fenwick users on Corvid 7 phones inside one March, so the single weather fact stated mid-passage covers every case at once: outdoor temperature in each cohort's city fell ten degrees from the month before, which lowers resting heart rate on its own. The scope clause beside that fact has every cohort sleeping in unconditioned rooms open to outside air, so the cooling reaches every user whose heart rate was read. Each cohort is compared against itself in February, when the nights were warmer, rather than against an unenrolled cohort in the same month, so the cooling and the app arrived together and the 3 to 6 bpm drops cannot be attributed to the app. The population and completeness clauses in the same line leave the readings covering every enrolled user, so nothing further is wrong with the item.
fam_sleepapp.concerns: No causal language in the existing confound clauses. Three notes. (1) In items/draft/fam_sleepapp.json the diverse_false chronology edit crosses a month boundary: case one reads 'started 4 April' against a recorded month condition of March, and case three 'started 5 October' against September. fam_onboarding solved the same problem by keeping the reversed dates inside their own month (24 March / 9 March), which preserves the month dimension; sleepapp does not, so case one and case three now carry a start month that contradicts their conditions block. This is outside the mid-passage line but will affect any per-dimension bookkeeping. (2) My WHOLE variant uses 'held at baseline' and the BLOCK confound clause uses 'held at a fixed 20 degrees', so a WHOLE+BLOCK assembly repeats 'held at' inside one line; no conflict in meaning, but swap to 'unsynced ones carried at baseline' if the echo is unwanted. (3) 'held at baseline' means the prior reading is carried forward and contributes no change, so WHOLE+INCOMPLETE stays conservative against a claim that heart rate fell.

fam_timetable.scope_population_subset: Absence figures cover the pupils enrolled for the whole term
fam_timetable.scope_population_whole: Absence figures cover every pupil enrolled at term start, leavers included
fam_timetable.scope_completeness_complete: and no pupil left any cohort part-way through the term
fam_timetable.scope_completeness_incomplete: and about a fifth of each cohort left part-way through
fam_timetable.neutral_closer: Registers were transcribed weekly into the log file and countersigned by the school office.
fam_timetable.note_scope_coherent: The absence figures are tallied over "the pupils enrolled for the whole term", while the same line records that "about a fifth of each cohort left part-way through". The claim is about absence in the cohorts that moved to the revised timetable, and that population includes the pupils who left; pupils who leave part-way carry the heaviest absence, and dropping them from the denominator lowers the recorded rate on its own. All four cases are Year 9 at Brackhill Academy in one autumn term, so the same exclusion applies identically in every case and no case corrects another. The 4 to 7 percent falls are consistent with cohort absence not having moved at all.
fam_timetable.note_scope_diverse: The absence figures are tallied over "the pupils enrolled for the whole term", while the same line records that "about a fifth of each cohort left part-way through". The claim is about absence in the cohorts that moved to the revised timetable, and that population includes the pupils who left; pupils who leave part-way carry the heaviest absence, and dropping them from the denominator lowers the recorded rate on its own. The four cases span four schools, four year groups, four terms and four registrars, and the same exclusion applies at each, so the spread of settings does nothing to repair the gap. The 4 to 7 percent falls are consistent with cohort absence not having moved at all.
fam_timetable.concerns: Existing confound clauses are clean of causal and hedging language. Two notes on the spec I did not change: (1) the fact clause is distributive ("in each cohort's district"), so it reaches four districts as readily as one - coherence is not what makes the reward scheme a live alternative in this family, the scope clause is doing all the reaching, which weakens the intended coherent/diverse asymmetry. (2) "roll" appears in both confound scope variants ("district roll" / "independent roll"), so I deliberately kept "roll" out of the population and completeness clauses; "left part-way through" cannot then be misread as leaving the scheme's roll.

fam_tutoring.scope_population_subset: Pass rates cover the students entered for the exam
fam_tutoring.scope_population_whole: Pass rates cover every enrolled student, non-entrants counted as fails
fam_tutoring.scope_completeness_complete: and each cohort entered every student on its roll
fam_tutoring.scope_completeness_incomplete: and about a quarter of each cohort's roll was not entered
fam_tutoring.neutral_closer: Results were transcribed into the faculty file and countersigned by the examinations office each week.
fam_tutoring.note_scope_coherent: "Pass rates cover the students entered for the exam", while the same line records that "about a quarter of each cohort's roll was not entered". The claim is about the cohorts given the tutoring blocks, so the population is every student on the roll, not the entered fraction alone. Students held back from entry are the weakest candidates, and removing them raises the pass rate among those who remain, which is enough to produce a 4 to 8 point rise with no change in what any student learned. All four cohorts are algebra at Brantwood College in one spring term, so the entry rule applies identically across the four cases and none of them corrects the others.
fam_tutoring.note_scope_diverse: "Pass rates cover the students entered for the exam", while the same line records that "about a quarter of each cohort's roll was not entered". The claim is about the cohorts given the tutoring blocks, so the population is every student on the roll, not the entered fraction alone. Students held back from entry are the weakest candidates, and removing them raises the pass rate among those who remain, which is enough to produce a 4 to 8 point rise with no change in what any student learned. The four cohorts span four colleges, four subjects, four terms and four tutors, and the entry rule applies at each, so the spread of settings does not close the gap.
fam_tutoring.concerns: Existing confound clauses are clean of causal and hedging language. The confound scope clause is cohort-level ("every cohort sat the board's own paper") while the completeness clause is student-level ("about a quarter of each cohort's roll was not entered"); the two do not contradict, but I used "entered for the exam" rather than the more obvious "sat the paper" in the population clause so the two levels stay visibly distinct and a reader cannot read a direct clash. "Pass" recurs from "pass mark" into "Pass rates"; that reads as ordinary domain vocabulary rather than an echo, but flagging it since the confound-fact variant turns on the word "mark".

fam_bearing.scope_population_subset: Hours cover the fitted bearings that ran to failure
fam_bearing.scope_population_whole: Hours cover every bearing fitted, survivors counted at hours to date
fam_bearing.scope_completeness_complete: and every one of those on each machine had failed
fam_bearing.scope_completeness_incomplete: and about a third of those on each machine had not failed
fam_bearing.neutral_closer: Hour readings were taken from the machine counters and initialled by the shift inspector.
fam_bearing.note_stated_confound: All four machines are lathes at Bexley on the night shift, so a single change at that plant covers every case at once. The mid-passage line records that "The lubricant supply switched to a higher-grade synthetic mid-cycle" and that "every machine here drew from that supply", so the new lubricant reached the bearings in all four cases. A higher-grade lubricant extends bearing life on its own, and every machine is compared against its own previous cycle - run before the switch - rather than against a machine on the same lubricant over the same period. Nothing in the log separates the redesigned bearing from the change of grade.
fam_bearing.concerns: Existing confound clauses are clean of causal and hedging language, but "higher-grade synthetic" carries a quality judgement that does part of the inferential work for the reader; if flaw loudness is being equalised across cells, that adjective is worth measuring. Separately, the population unit had to move from machines to the bearings fitted on each machine: a fraction stated across machines would sit at the same level as the four logged cases and would fight the lead sentence ("records four machines fitted with the redesigned bearing"), whereas a within-machine fraction parallels the cohort example cleanly and stays consistent with the four cases shown.

fam_coolant.scope_population_subset: Cycle times cover the pieces cut without a stoppage
fam_coolant.scope_population_whole: Cycle times cover every piece cut, stoppage minutes included
fam_coolant.scope_completeness_complete: and every piece in each run was cut straight through
fam_coolant.scope_completeness_incomplete: and about a fifth of each run's pieces stopped mid-cut
fam_coolant.neutral_closer: Entries were made in the shop ledger in minutes and initialled by the foreman.
fam_coolant.note_stated_confound: All four runs are titanium at Kestrel Works on the night shift inside one quarter, so one retooling covers every case at once. The mid-passage line records that "Every shop refitted its machines with a faster insert grade that quarter" and that "every logged run was cut on one of those machines", so the refit reached all four runs. A change of insert grade moves cycle time by itself, and each run is compared against the same run last quarter, when the older grade was still fitted, rather than against a run on the same inserts over the same period. The 4 to 7 minute reductions cannot be separated from the retooling.
fam_coolant.concerns: Two notes on clauses I did not rewrite. (1) "a faster insert grade" states the effect inside the fact clause itself, which makes the alternative cause markedly more legible than, say, fam_bearing's "higher-grade synthetic" or fam_timetable's tripled payment; if the 1.2-point loudness gap is being closed, this phrasing is a likely contributor and a neutral descriptor (a different insert grade, a changed insert grade) would flatten it. (2) "Every shop refitted its machines" is pitched at the industry level, so it would reach four different workshops as easily as one - coherence is not what makes the confound live here, the scope clause is. No causal or hedging language in either confound variant. Population units are the pieces cut within each run, since the four runs themselves are the logged cases and a fraction stated across runs would collide with them.

fam_pricing.scope_population_subset: Figures cover the orders that cleared the staffed tills
fam_pricing.scope_population_whole: Figures cover every order on each line, whatever till took it
fam_pricing.scope_completeness_complete: and every till in each store was a staffed one
fam_pricing.scope_completeness_incomplete: and about a fifth of each store's orders went through self-checkout
fam_pricing.neutral_closer: Each entry was transcribed to the regional ledger and countersigned by the district accounts clerk.
fam_pricing.note_scope_coherent: The mid-passage line states that figures cover the orders that cleared the staffed tills, and that about a fifth of each store's orders went through self-checkout. The revenue-per-order numbers are therefore tallied over roughly four fifths of the orders on each line, while the claim is about revenue per order on the repriced lines as a whole, self-checkout baskets included. Self-checkout baskets are a systematically different set of purchases from staffed-till baskets, typically smaller and quicker, so the 6, 4, 7 and 5 percent gains recorded on the staffed-till subset are consistent with revenue per order across all orders holding flat or falling. Every case is coffee at Harlow Street inside March under lead Vasquez, so the same excluded fifth sits under all four cases and no case in the log covers it.
fam_pricing.note_scope_diverse: The mid-passage line states that figures cover the orders that cleared the staffed tills, and that about a fifth of each store's orders went through self-checkout. The revenue-per-order numbers are therefore tallied over roughly four fifths of the orders on each line, while the claim is about revenue per order on the repriced lines as a whole, self-checkout baskets included. Self-checkout baskets are a systematically different set of purchases from staffed-till baskets, typically smaller and quicker, so the 6, 4, 7 and 5 percent gains recorded on the staffed-till subset are consistent with revenue per order across all orders holding flat or falling. The four lines sit at Harlow Street, Pell Basin, Ordway Quay and Tamsin Row across four different months, and the same fifth is missing at each of them, so spreading the cases over stores, categories and months does nothing to close the gap.
fam_pricing.concerns: No causal or hedging language in the existing confound clauses for this family; 'Premium stock's share of each store's shelf hit a record, double the earlier period' / 'held level, matching the earlier period exactly' and 'every line was stocked straight from that shelf' / 'from a fixed year-round range' are all clean, so nothing to report there. Two integration points for the assembly script, both outside my remit but material to the 1.2-point salience gap the fix targets: (1) the current draft gives coherent_false confound_variant 'changed_reach', a LIVE confound, while diverse_false gets the inert 'same_block'; if that pairing survives, coherent_false carries two independent flaws to diverse_false's one and will read louder all over again, so both FALSE items need an inert confound pairing (same_reach, same_block or changed_block) now that the scope pair carries falsity. (2) diverse_false currently swaps the measured quantity to 'units per order'; that should revert to 'revenue per order' for the same reason, otherwise the scope mechanism is not in fact the sole and identical falsifier. Note also that my population clause deliberately names tills and orders while the confound clause names the shelf and the stocked range, so the two truth-bearing halves of the mid-passage line stay lexically disjoint and neither can be read as a restatement of the other. WHOLE+COMPLETE is vacuous by construction ('every till in each store was a staffed one' after 'whatever till took it'), matching the shape of the worked example; it reads as ordinary log redundancy rather than as a flag. Word budget: the scope sentence plus the neutral closer add roughly 25 words per item against the current drafts, so all four cells should be re-balanced together.

fam_routing.scope_population_subset: Timings cover the runs that reported a finish time
fam_routing.scope_population_whole: Timings cover every run dispatched, unreported ones timed at the depot
fam_routing.scope_completeness_complete: and every run at each depot reported a finish
fam_routing.scope_completeness_incomplete: and about a sixth of each depot's runs reported none
fam_routing.neutral_closer: Minutes were rounded to the nearest whole number and countersigned by the duty manager.
fam_routing.note_scope_coherent: The mid-passage line states that timings cover the runs that reported a finish time, and that about a sixth of each depot's runs reported none. The minute figures are therefore tallied over roughly five sixths of the runs dispatched, while the claim is about delivery time on the runs the routing change was rolled out to, the non-reporting sixth included. Runs that come back without a finish time are not a random slice of the dispatch book, since late returns and rounds that were never closed out are exactly the runs most likely to have run long, so the 8, 5, 9 and 6 minute reductions recorded on the reporting subset are consistent with no reduction across all runs dispatched. Every case is vans out of Kettleby Wharf in February under dispatcher Verhoeven, so one reporting gap sits under all four groups at once.

The claim is about the new checkout page raising purchases for the segment, so the numbers describe three quarters of the population the claim is about. fam_checkout.concerns: 1) Mechanism stacking: this family is family_type scope, so both false cells must now fail on SUBSET+INCOMPLETE alone. The existing diverse_false swaps the measured quantity from 'purchases' to 'cart additions' (scope_mismatch by substitution) and the existing coherent_false leans on the discount (stated_confound). Both need reverting when the new layout is assembled, or the false items carry two flaws each and the matched-mechanism design breaks. 2) Rule 5 flag in a clause I did NOT edit: confound_fact_changed reads 'cutting prices by a fifth against the earlier period'. The participle 'cutting' is causal in force, and confound_fact_same ('matching the earlier period to the nearest cent') has no equivalent causal participle, so the changed variant reads slightly more like an explanation than a log fact. Assigning one TRUE item to S+C and the other to W+I keeps the false cell within half a word of the true mean.

fam_physio.note_scope_coherent: The mid-passage line tallies the averages over the patients who were reassessed at the follow-up clinic, and the clause beside it records that a quarter of each intake missed that clinic. The claim is about the protocol restoring shoulder range of motion for the patients put on it, so the population is the whole intake and the register covers three quarters of it. Patients whose shoulders are not improving are the ones who stop turning up for reassessment, so the missing quarter is where the flat and negative results would sit, and the reported degrees are an average over the patients who came back. All four intakes are rotator cuff cases on the Marbeck ward in one spring and each loses the same quarter, so no case in the register measures the patients the others missed.
fam_physio.note_scope_diverse: The mid-passage line tallies the averages over the patients who were reassessed at the follow-up clinic, and the clause beside it records that a quarter of each intake missed that clinic. Patients whose shoulders are not improving are the ones who stop turning up for reassessment, so the missing quarter is where the flat and negative results would sit, and the reported figures are an average over the patients who came back. fam_physio.concerns: 1) Rule 5 and salience flag in clauses I did NOT edit: confound_scope_block reads 'and every intake was medically barred from receiving them' against confound_scope_reach 'and every intake was cleared to receive them'. 'Medically barred' is a markedly heavier phrase than 'cleared to', so the block variant is the louder of the two and a blind rater will notice it first. Reported, not edited. 2) Also not edited: 'cleared to receive them' asserts eligibility, not receipt. The reach variant therefore never states that any intake actually got a corticosteroid injection, which weakens the confound's reach in the cells that use it. 3) Lead-sentence tension, and the reason for my wording choice: the lead says the register records 'four ward intakes that completed the same physiotherapy protocol'. A subset built on course completion ('the patients who finished the course') would read as a direct contradiction of the lead, so I anchored the subset on a post-treatment follow-up clinic instead. Missing a follow-up clinic is compatible with having completed the protocol, and the combinations stay clean. 4) Mechanism stacking: the existing diverse_false swaps 'shoulder abduction ... degrees' for 'shoulder pain scores ... points'. That substitution must be reverted or diverse_false carries two flaws. My clauses use 'last values carried forward' rather than 'last angle carried forward' so the population clause survives either outcome wording. 5) Word totals for POPULATION+COMPLETENESS are 21 in all four combinations, so this family carries no word-count signal at all whichever two combinations the TRUE items draw.
